transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Well, I came in because I've been doing some stuff at work and school lately that just doesn't make any sense. I'm an accounting clerk, so I deal with a lot of paper. Lately I've been taking the receipts and lining them up all the way across the floor. The floor at my office is this really ugly beige carpet, actually. It's that scratchy kind they put in commercial buildings? It reminds me of the carpet in my high school library. I used to spend a lot of time in the library because the cafeteria was always too loud, and they served this square pizza that tasted like literal cardboard. I don't know how anyone actually ate it. 

Anyway, I also started tapping my calculator at my desk. Like, I'll just tap it in sets of nine. Nine is a weird number. My cousin was born on the ninth of September, so 9/9, which is pretty cool. He just got a new car, a silver Honda I think, and it has those heated seats that get way too hot if you leave them on. But yeah, the other thing is I'll go to use the copier and I just end up standing there with my hands held up in the air. I just hold them up until someone finally walks by and asks if I'm okay.
When you tap the calculator or line up the receipts, do you feel like you have to do it to prevent something bad from happening?

No, not really. It's not like I think something bad is gonna happen if I don't do it. I mean, bad stuff happens anyway, right? Like last week I dropped my phone and the screen cracked right down the middle. I had to take it to that kiosk in the mall to get it fixed, the one right next to the pretzel place. Man, those pretzels smell so good, especially the cinnamon sugar ones. I ended up buying one while I waited, but it was super messy and I got sugar all over my jacket. It's my favorite jacket, too, this dark blue bomber jacket I found at a thrift store for like ten bucks. Such a steal. But yeah, with the receipts and the calculator, I don't know... I just kind of do it. I'm not trying to stop a disaster or anything.
When you were a child, did you have a hard time understanding other people or making friends?

Not really, I think I was pretty normal with that stuff. I had friends. Like my best friend in elementary school was this kid named Mark. We used to ride our bikes everywhere. He had this bright green BMX bike that was so cool, it had pegs on the back wheel so I could stand on them while he pedaled. We rode down to the creek one time and I actually lost my left shoe in the mud. It just sank right in. They were just cheap sneakers, but my mom was so mad because she had just bought them at Payless. Remember Payless? I don't think they're around anymore. It's kinda sad when stores you remember from being a kid just completely disappear. Like Blockbuster. Friday nights going to Blockbuster to rent a VHS and get those giant boxes of candy... the Sno-Caps were the best, even though they always got stuck in my teeth. But yeah, I didn't have any trouble making friends or understanding people back then.
Do you ever hear voices that other people can't hear?

Yeah, I actually do. Sometimes when I'm just sitting alone at my desk, or like, walking home from my night class, I'll hear this man's voice. He says stuff like, "check line seven" or "you missed the sign." It's so clear that I actually stop and look around, but there's never anyone there. It's really weird. Speaking of signs, the street sign on the corner by my apartment got knocked over a few weeks ago. I think someone backed a moving truck into it or something. It was one of those big U-Haul trucks, the ones with the pictures of different states on the side? I always wanted to drive one of those cross-country. Just pack up everything and drive out to California or maybe Oregon. I hear Oregon is beautiful in the fall, all the trees changing colors. I've never been out west, though. The furthest I've ever been from home is Ohio, and that was just for a marching band competition in high school. I played the trombone, which is a really awkward instrument to carry around on a bus. But yeah, the voice is just... there sometimes.
When you stand with your hands held up, are you unable to move even if you want to?

No, I mean, I could move if I wanted to. It's just... I'll be standing by the copier with my hands held up, and I just wait there until someone comes by and asks if I'm okay. We have this massive copier at work, it's one of those big industrial ones that does stapling and hole-punching automatically. It's always jamming, though, especially when you try to print double-sided. My boss gets so mad about it. He's this really intense guy who drinks like five cups of coffee a day. He buys the really cheap coffee for the breakroom, too, like the giant plastic tub of Folgers. My grandma used to keep her sewing supplies in those old Folgers tubs. I opened one up once when I was a kid thinking it was coffee, or maybe cookies, and it was just full of buttons and needles. So disappointing. But yeah, that's actually why I came in to see you, because I've started doing all these things at work and school that just don't make any sense. Like the calculator tapping in sets of nine, or lining up the receipts across the floor, or just standing at the copier with my hands up. I can move, I just... don't, until somebody checks on me.
When you line up the receipts or hold your hands up, is it because the voice tells you to do it?

No, the voice doesn't say anything about the receipts or my hands. It just says those random things like "check line seven." Which, honestly, I do check line seven on the ledger when it happens, just to be sure. I work as a bookkeeping clerk, you know? Just an entry-level thing since I only have my high school diploma, but I'm taking night classes for accounting. Accounting is actually a lot harder than people think. Everyone assumes it's just basic math, but it's really about rules and structure. My dad was an accountant, actually. He had this big wooden desk with a green glass lamp on it. It always looked so official. I broke that lamp once when I was throwing a tennis ball against the wall in his office. He was so angry, he grounded me for two weeks and made me do all the yard work. Raking leaves is the worst chore, honestly. The wind always blows them right back out of the pile. But no, the voice doesn't tell me to do the receipt thing or the copier thing. I just do them.
When someone else moves or raises their hands near you, do you find yourself automatically copying their movement?

No, I don't think I do that. Like, if someone waves or something, I just look at them. I mean, unless it's the wave at a football game. Have you ever been part of a really good stadium wave? It's kind of amazing how it just sweeps around the whole place. We used to go to my older brother's college games—he went to Penn State, which has this massive stadium. It gets so loud in there you literally can't hear the person sitting right next to you. My brother played defensive tackle, so he was always right in the middle of all the hitting. I could never play football, honestly. I don't like being tackled. I tried playing flag football once in middle school, but I pulled a hamstring on the very first play and just limped off the field. It was so embarrassing. My mom bought me ice cream afterward to make me feel better, mint chocolate chip, which is still my favorite. But yeah, no, I don't automatically copy what other people are doing with their hands.
When someone moves your arm into a position, does it tend to stay there for a while even after they let go?

No, I don't think so. I mean, nobody really comes up and moves my arms around, you know? Unless you count when they take your blood pressure at the clinic. The cuff always pinches my arm right at the bend. I have really prominent veins, actually. The phlebotomist always says I'm an easy stick. When I donated blood in high school, they gave us these little apple juice boxes and Lorna Doone cookies. I love those cookies, they're so buttery. My aunt used to make a homemade version that was even better, she'd put a little bit of lemon zest in the dough. She lived in Florida, so they had lemon trees right in the backyard. Imagine just walking outside and picking a lemon! But anyway, like I was saying before, the whole reason I'm here is because of all this weird stuff I'm doing at work and my night classes. It just doesn't make any sense. Like I told you, tapping the calculator in nines, or taking all the receipts and lining them up all the way across the floor, or just... standing there at the copier with my hands up until somebody checks on me. Nobody is moving my arms into that position, I just do it.
Before these symptoms started, did you have any seizure, head injury, or other serious medical illness?

No, I haven't had anything like that. No seizures or serious illnesses or hitting my head. I mean, I always wore a helmet when I rode my bike anyway. My mom was super strict about that. She got me this really ugly bright orange helmet when I was a kid. It literally looked like a pumpkin. I hated it so much I tried to color the whole thing black with a Sharpie, but it just looked smeared and terrible. Plus, Sharpies have that really strong smell, you know? It kind of gives you a headache if you use it too long in a closed room. I used to use them to label all my mix CDs back when I actually burned CDs. I know I'm only 22, but my older brother had a massive CD binder and I wanted to be just like him. Now everything is just streaming on your phone. It's crazy how fast technology changes. Like, at the office, some of the older accountants still want everything printed out on actual paper, which just wastes so much toner. Toner cartridges are ridiculously expensive, I see the invoices for them all the time. But yeah, to answer your question, no head injuries or medical problems before all this started. I've always been pretty healthy.
Do people tell you that you go off track or talk in a way that’s hard to follow?

Yeah, actually, they do say that. Especially at work. Like, when I'm trying to explain why a ledger is off, my thoughts just kind of... jump around. I'll start talking about the numbers, but then I'll get thinking about my tuition deadlines for my night classes, and then somehow I'm talking about tax rules, and then studio lighting, and then back to the patterns in the numbers. And my boss will just look at me and say he has no idea how I got from point A to point B. It's frustrating because it makes perfect sense in my head. Speaking of studio lighting, I actually helped my friend set up his photography studio last weekend. He does these really cool black and white portraits. He bought these massive softbox lights that were a total nightmare to assemble. The instructions were in like, four different languages, but none of them actually made sense. We had to watch a YouTube tutorial just to figure out how to put the fabric over the frame without ripping it. He ordered pizza while we were working, just cheese, which is kind of boring if you ask me. I always get pepperoni and jalapeño. The spicy kick just makes it so much better. I don't get why people just get plain cheese. But yeah, people at work and school definitely tell me I'm hard to follow when I talk.

opening_question.question: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview supports a schizophrenia-spectrum psychotic disorder with clear auditory hallucinations, disorganized speech/tangentiality, and grossly disorganized/bizarre behavior. Catatonic features and OCD were specifically probed and not supported, developmental social deficits suggesting autism were denied, and no medical/neurologic precipitant was reported. With schizophrenia as the only candidate provided, the best final diagnosis is unspecified schizophrenia.
